displayOrder.name: Pokédex and Preview
displayOrder.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create a realistic, production-quality PokeTaskBar macOS desktop COLLECTION page. Attached image 1 is the approved Today window and pixel-art Lapras reference; image 2 is the approved Projects Grid surface styling; image 3 is the CURRENT compact Collection screen, provided only to ground its existing Pokédex features, not as the main-window layout. This is the large desktop app window.
Target 1488 x 1056, landscape straight-on complete native window. Current date Friday 18 September 2026 if any date is shown. No presentation titles, numbers, external browser, poster text or layout annotations.
Preserve approved expanded left navigation approximately 240px: PokeTaskBar identity; Cody; Search; Today, Focus, Issues, Projects, Initiatives, Collection, Usage; Settings at bottom. Collection selected. Native traffic lights, back/forward controls, compact Collection page tab, left/right sidebar-collapse controls. Navigation and optional extras independently resizable/collapsible.
Shared style: continuous #EFF0F2 shell; pale #F8F8FA main rounded canvas inset with open gutters on ALL edges, visible lower corners; white grouped content surfaces, ink #242528, metadata #73757B, restrained blue selection. Neutral SF Pro-like typography at readable 14-16pt and modest 28-32pt page heading. Pixel-art Pokémon provide colour; surrounding UI stays quiet. NO permanent sidebar separator strokes, full-height rules, major edge-to-edge horizontal dividers or grip dots. Hover guides are invisible at rest.
Keep Collection's existing destinations Bag, Storage, Pokédex, Shop in one compact labelled local navigation row; Pokédex selected. Inside Pokédex retain a quiet Pokédex / Catch log view choice. Do not add these to the main left sidebar. Include modest Find a Pokémon search, a Rarity filter, and Shiny filter. Show '12 species' as a quiet count; no celebratory metric cards, streaks, XP charts, battle stats, marketplace, trading, purchases or new reward systems.
Mock owned species: #001 Bulbasaur, #004 Charmander, #007 Squirtle, #025 Pikachu, #037 Vulpix, #054 Psyduck, #094 Gengar, #129 Magikarp, #131 Lapras, #133 Eevee, #143 Snorlax, #149 Dragonite. Use recognizable crisp proportional Pokémon pixel sprites, not smooth 3D toys. All twelve are collected; no locked silhouettes. Lapras is selected and currently Raising, rarity Rare, level 32 illustrative. Preserve same Lapras appearance as approved Today. Keep counts consistent. Only Lapras needs a rarity badge; do not invent classifications for others.
Main workflow is browsing the collection, inspecting a Pokémon, and choosing a representative. Use the precise action 'Set representative' and a secondary 'View details' where useful; do not confuse this with training, swapping the active companion or trading. Main selected-Pokémon actions remain usable with optional right extras hidden. Today retains the main companion dashboard hero; Collection is a useful browsable archive. Avoid making every property a card. Generous spacing and sharp type, no clipped content.

Show a clean 4-column by 3-row grid of all twelve species, ordered by the numbers in the shared brief. Each small rounded cell has a muted species number at top-left, crisp centered sprite roughly 65px tall, and readable name below. Light surfaces with extremely subtle outlines, not trading-card frames. Lapras in row 3 column 1 is selected with a neutral blue-tinted background and tiny Raising badge. No heavy shadows or thick borders. Keep every tile same height.
Below the grid reserve one compact selected-item action strip containing '#131 Lapras · Rare' and the dark Set representative button, plus a quieter View details link. This strip is in the MAIN canvas and remains when extras hide.
Right extras contain a single white rounded preview panel: larger Lapras around 170px, name, #131, small Rare and Raising labels, Level 32, and a brief quiet line 'Your current companion'. No duplicate action buttons or invented metrics here. Leave the rest of the right rail open. The main task is browsing a beautiful, calm collection while previewing a selection.
